mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met, or the trigger fails to produce statistically significant negative returns at the 5% level in a walk-forward test.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand but a nascent housing recovery, which historically precedes a mild equity correction over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > previous 3-month average
regime_hint: late-cycle demand slowdown with housing stabilization
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the predictive relationship reverses during a housing boom.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months is associated with reduced consumer confidence and corporate earnings pressure, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when this trigger is met in at least 70% of out-of-sample tests, or the trigger fires but returns are positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below -1% for four consecutive months signals a broad-based contraction in economic activity, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month -1% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the relationship fails to hold during a supply-chain normalization period.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in real personal savings (RSAFS) and a fall in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a shift from spending to saving, which historically precedes equity market weakness over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases AND GDPC1 decreases for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when this trigger is met, or the trigger occurs without a market reaction in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate below 2% during a recessionary environment signals an aggressive easing cycle, which typically supports equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when this trigger is met, or the trigger fires but returns are negative more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth above 0.5% month-over-month for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which historically coincides with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > 0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when this trigger is met, or the trigger occurs without a positive market reaction in more than 50% of episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average while GDP growth (GDPC1) remains flat signals a housing-led demand recovery that typically precedes positive equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average AND GDPC1 change ≈ 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when this trigger is met, or the trigger occurs without a positive market reaction in more than 60% of cases.
